_note: PURGED AND REBUILT 2026-08-23 (Ben): the hot file holds only the items of the earliest incomplete sprint - Sprint 16, the mercenary vertical slice (v0.1.15). Every item that existed before (530, ids <= BL-568) is snapshotted verbatim in archive/backlog-purged-2026-08-23.json and is NOT open work. New items name their sprint in `sprint`. File nothing here that the open sprint does not need; when the sprint closes, the next sprint's items are authored fresh against the authority docs. Ids never reuse.
Canonical backlog for Project Io — the authoritative METADATA index of every backlog item.
One item = one object in `items`.
STATUS (authoritative; JSON wins over any prose/glyph disagreement):
designed    (glyph ✓) — design settled, promote-ready.
design-owed (glyph ~) — design still owed; must be settled before promotion.
PRIORITY (ascending): F C B A S SSS.
F=deferred/parked, C=low, B=medium, A=important, S=high, SSS=do-immediately.
`parked:true` is the explicit flag for F-priority items.
DIFFICULTY (1-5): 1=~5min, 2=~20min, 3=~1h, 4=~3h, 5=~12h+ (break a 5 down).
SEQUENCING: `requires` lists BL-XXX ids of backlog items that must land first (supercedes the
old `waits_on` short_name list — v2 schema 2026-06-17). `blocked_on` names a truly-external
prerequisite with no backlog item (third-party dep, real-world gate). An item can be `designed`
and still have unmet `requires`. Both fields are nullable; [] means no dependencies.
WORKFLOW: a `designed` item is PROMOTED into REFINED.md and DELIVERED (see DELIVERY.md).
A `design-owed` item is DESIGNED first (prose settled in `design` field, status flipped).
When work lands, the item is RETAINED here under the terminal status `complete` with a
resolution/completion_note, and design propagates into the authority doc. (Convention updated
2026-07-04: terminal items were once removed; the tooling — gyre.py, progress counts — now
depends on them staying. Do not delete landed entries.)
(Terminal status normalised 2026-08-01: `complete` is the only one. `shipped` was a
synonym with no defined difference — written only by tools/session/ship_items.js and
apply_session_close.js, which now write `complete`; the six items carrying it were
converted. Readers still tolerate the old value, so nothing breaks on an old branch.)
DESIGN PROSE — the `design` field (policy updated 2026-06-17):
- ALL items: prose lives in the `design` field here, not in BACKLOG.md.
- NEW items: author prose here directly. No BACKLOG.md body.
- LEGACY items (pre-2026-06-17): `design: "@BACKLOG.md"` means prose is still in markdown.
Migrate to this field on first edit (design settle or promotion) — do not wait for promotion.
On migration: write prose here, replace the BACKLOG.md body with a tombstone line.
- ON PROMOTION into REFINED.md: delete any remaining BACKLOG.md body (if not yet migrated).
- BACKLOG.md therefore only drains, never grows, and is deleted once empty.
- For designs with rich tables use markdown in the `design` string (tables render fine).
- `design: "@<doc>"` is also valid as a pointer to an authority doc when prose lives there.
VERSION GOAL (policy added 2026-07-08): every NEW item names which version it is FOR via the
`version_goal` field — the minor it targets ("v0.0.9"), the next one ("v0.1.0"), or
"post-v0.1.0" for anything beyond the prototype's remaining arc (see ROADMAP.md for the
live version sequence and themes). This is a goal, not a promise — it may slip a version at
re-sequencing, same as priority. Legacy items predating this policy are not backfilled; treat
a missing `version_goal` as "unset (legacy)", not as "post-v0.1.0".
ARCHIVE — the hot/cold split (policy added 2026-08-02):
This file is the METADATA INDEX and is read ACROSS items far more often than INTO one.
So when an item lands, its narrative fields — design, resolution, completion_note,
progress_note — MOVE OUT to docs/development/archive/backlog-design-<quarter>.json.
The item keeps `design: "@<that path>"` (the pointer form blessed above) plus an
`archived` field naming the cold file. This is the authority time-slice made physical:
backlog.json owns the item while it is open; the cold store and the subject authority
doc own it once it has landed.
- Run it: tools/session/archive_designs.js (Delivery close step, after ship_items.js).
- Read it back: tools/session/backlog_query.js --full, or backlog_view.js — both resolve
the pointer transparently, so an archived item reads exactly like a hot one.
- Reverse it: archive_designs.js --restore [BL-XXX ...]. Nothing is ever deleted.
- AMEND A LANDED ITEM'S PROSE IN THE COLD FILE, not here — the hot file has no copy.
- backlog_lint.js FAILS on an `archived` pointer with no record behind it, and WARNS
when frozen history climbs back over 30% of this file.
AUTHOR (policy added 2026-08-22): items may carry an `author` field naming who
proposed the item (e.g. "Joe"). Informational only — no effect on status, priority,
or workflow. Nullable; missing/null means unattributed (legacy items). Design
brainstorms that haven't yet become a backlog item live in docs/development/design/.

Buildings draw OVER the hex, not on a plate of their own - and a stacked tile says which kinds
items.design:
## Ben's words
> "Remove building background. Buildings should be drawn over the hex, not completely on
> top. We also need a way to represent multiple types of buildings on the same tile."

## Two halves, and only the second needs a decision

**The plate goes.** A building marker currently paints its own background before its glyph,
so the tile's terrain, texture and lens wash all stop at the marker's edge. The hex is the
thing that carries substrate, cover, ownership and every lens; occluding it to draw a glyph
trades away the map to label it. The glyph draws over the hex and the hex keeps showing.
Legibility then rests on the glyph's own stroke and its contrast against a live background,
which is what the icon vocabulary is for.

**The stack does not have an answer yet.** Building stacks on one tile landed with the
richness-derived cap (BL-193, building stack capacity), so N is not two - it is whatever the
tile's richness allows, and the tile currently shows one marker regardless. Three shapes are
on the table and this item does not pick one:
  1. **A cluster.** Up to k glyphs arranged inside the hex, shrinking as k grows. Reads
     exactly at k=2-3 and becomes soup past that.
  2. **Primary plus count.** The dominant kind at full size with a small `x3`. Always legible,
     never says WHICH three.
  3. **A segmented ring.** One arc per kind around the hex edge, glyph in the middle for the
     dominant kind. Scales further than the cluster and costs a new visual idiom.

The choice is Ben's and is the item's real content. Whatever wins must survive the coarse-fill
threshold the canvas already applies - below it a hex draws no detail at all, so the stack
read has to degrade to something, not vanish.

## Not in scope
Which buildings exist, how many a tile may hold, and what a stack shares - all settled by the
stack-capacity work. This is the render.

## RULED (Ben, 2026-08-24, the Sprint 17b design form)
> Stack glyph: **Segmented ring.**

One arc per building kind around the hex edge, with the dominant kind's glyph in the middle. Chosen over the cluster (which becomes soup past three) and over primary-plus-count (which is always legible but never says WHICH kinds) - the ring is the only one of the three that scales with the richness-derived stack cap and still names its contents.

**Two things the ring has to get right, neither optional.** It is a new visual idiom, so it must not collide with the vocabulary already on the hex - the province edge stroke and the corp-border pass both live at the same rim. And it must DEGRADE rather than vanish below the coarse-fill threshold: at that size there is no rim to segment, so the fallback is the dominant kind's glyph alone, not an empty hex.

The plate removal is unaffected and unblocked: the glyph draws over live terrain either way.

items.title: The land stops smearing: what reads as blurred texture is the province blend
items.design:
## Ben's words
> "Texture / Land diffusion turns into a blur, it should definitely be crisper than this."

## Measured before changing anything (Rule 0b), and it is not the texture pass
`scripts/verify/zoom_ladder.lua` walks the canvas's four LOD bands at one spot:
coarse fill below 7px circumradius, hexes with no texture below 14px, texture ramping
14-22px, full strength above 22px.

What the ladder shows:
  * **x1 and x2 are CRISP.** Coarse fill draws a distinct little block per tile and reads
    cleanly. The complaint is not about the far view.
  * **From ~x3.5 up, LAND loses its hex edges entirely** and becomes a continuous grey-brown
    smear with building and settlement glyphs floating in it.
  * **OCEAN stays crisp at every zoom**, hex outlines intact.

That split is the diagnosis. A faint texture pass would soften land and water alike; only
one thing in the canvas treats them differently, and it is **BL-511's province blend**
(`body_surface_canvas.cpp`, 'a hex's fill is blended into its province's, so the seams
INSIDE a province disappear'). Ocean tiles carry province id 0, are unpartitioned, and do
not blend - which is exactly why they are the only thing still showing a grid.

Provinces run 7-12 tiles since the repartition, so the blend is averaging colour across a
large cell rather than softening a seam. The texture constants are not implicated and
should not be touched first.

## This is a reversal of Ben's own recent ruling, and is his to make
The blend is not an accident: the code records it as **Ben's ruling of 2026-08-21** - 'a
blended gradient, explicitly not a dominant composition and not a texture pattern'. Three
days later the same treatment is being described as a blur. That is a legitimate change of
mind on seeing it at working zoom for the first time, and it is named here rather than
quietly tuned, because silently dialling back a dated ruling is how a design loses its
record.

Three shapes, and the third is where the rest of the 2026-08-24 list points:
  1. **Drop the blend.** Every tile draws its own colour; the province reads from its edge
     stroke alone. Maximum crispness, and the province stops being visible as a FIELD.
  2. **Confine it to the seam.** Blend only within a band near province vertices, so the
     interior of a cell stays flat and only the joins soften. Keeps the soft-cell read at a
     fraction of the smear.
  3. **Invert it - colour at the edge, clarity inside.** Which is precisely what BL-601 asks
     for at the NATION grain: 'borders extending their colour inwards', no diffusion. Same
     complaint, same mechanism, one grain apart - so answering the two together is cheaper
     than answering them separately, and more likely to be coherent.

## Not implicated, checked
The texture LOD floor (14px), the 22px full-strength ramp, and the 0.45 per-lens attenuation
are all working as designed. The lens rungs of the ladder show the same land smear with or
without a lens, so the attenuation is not compounding into the symptom either.

## This also answers a question that was explicitly held for it
BL-514 (blend all tiles) is on record as **held awaiting Ben's look** - his words, 2026-08-21:
*"I have a feeling that we should blend all tiles, not just within provinces, but hold off on
that until I see what it looks like with larger provinces."* Its design note goes further and
names the exact evidence to have ready: the map at PLAY zoom, where seam density is what
actually reads.

The provinces are now 7-12 tiles, Ben has looked at play zoom, and the verdict is 'blur'. So
the held question is answered - and answered in the OPPOSITE direction from the one it
proposed. BL-514 asked whether to remove the last remaining stop on the blend; the answer is
that the blend already reaches too far. That reversal should be recorded against BL-514 rather
than left as a held item nobody revisits.

## RULED (Ben, 2026-08-24, the Sprint 17b design form)
> "Just reduce the amount of smearing so it looks less blurred."

**The blend STAYS and is dialled back.** None of the three shapes offered - drop it, confine it to the seam, invert it - was taken. This is the smallest possible answer and it is a good one: the province blend is doing something Ben wants (a cell that reads as one shape), it is simply doing too much of it, and a magnitude is far cheaper to tune than a mechanism is to replace.

**What this changes about the item.** It stops being a redesign and becomes a constant with a name. The corner blend currently takes the flat mean of the tile and its same-province corner-sharing neighbours; the fix is to lerp that result back toward the tile's OWN fill by a named strength, so 1.0 is today's behaviour and 0.0 is no blend at all. Start near 0.35, then let Ben set it by eye in the live app - the target is his eye, not a number, so this ends at the keyboard (Rule 0b).

**It also decouples from BL-601.** The two were filed as one design because both looked like 'stop diffusing'. Under this ruling they are not: the province blend is a fill treatment that survives at reduced strength, and the national border is a separate always-on pass being rebuilt as an inward band. The `requires` is dropped.

**And it settles BL-514 (blend all tiles) in the negative.** That item asked whether to remove the last stop on the blend. The answer is that the blend already reaches too far.

## CORRECTION 2026-08-24 — BL-514 is not held, it LANDED, and it is the cause
Two paragraphs above say BL-514 (blend all tiles) is 'HELD awaiting Ben's look' and that this item settles it. That was read off BL-514's design prose, which still carries the held wording. **The prose is stale and the code is the authority.** BL-514 landed 2026-08-22 and is `complete`:

> `body_surface_canvas.cpp`, ~line 2330 - "BL-514 (Ben, 2026-08-22): the blend CROSSES province borders. The province-match term that used to stand here is deliberately gone - land is one continuous field now, and a province edge is drawn only as the selection outline."

> `body_surface_canvas.cpp`, ~line 2414 - "Province edge: NOT DRAWN ... Ben moved it to zero (BL-514, 2026-08-22): 'blur should cross province borders' ... the pass is gone rather than dialled down."

**So the sequence is three rulings, not two, and the middle one is the cause.** BL-511 blended WITHIN a province and stroked the edges. BL-514 removed the stop, so the blend crosses province borders and the edge stroke is gone entirely - land became one continuous field. BL-597 is Ben seeing THAT at working zoom and pulling it back. This item is not a reversal of the original province-grain design; it is a reversal of the 2026-08-22 widening.

**What changes in the work.** The constant is a LAND blend strength, not a province blend strength - there is no province qualifier left in the pass to name it after. Do not reinstate a province-match term: the global blend is intentional and is not what Ben objected to. The lerp is otherwise exactly as specified.

**And it explains why the ocean stayed crisp** in the zoom-ladder measurement: the blend needs `province != 0`, and ocean is unpartitioned. That was read at the time as evidence of a per-province blend. It is evidence of the ocean exclusion, which is a different thing.

The general lesson is the one already on the record: backlog design prose goes stale, and a landed item's CODE is what says what it did.

items.title: Province folds into the tile Selection element as one longer accordion, reordered
items.design:
## Ben's words
> "Province selection element must be bundled into the tile selection element. By this I
> mean, we just use a longer accordion. We can also swap the order. Buildings -> Deposits ->
> Resources -> Population -> Terrain. Keep the tile available buildings tab, and drop the
> province buildings tab."

## What changes
Today the band shows a province card and a tile card as two separate kinds, each with its own
paged centre pane - 'Terrain (1/3)', 'Tiles (1/3)' - stepped with prev/next arrows. This
replaces the pair with ONE element and swaps the pager idiom for an accordion, ordered
**Buildings, Deposits, Resources, Population, Terrain**. That order is itself the argument:
it runs from what the player can act on to what the ground merely is, where the pager's order
ran the other way.

The tile's available-buildings tab stays. The province buildings tab goes - it was the same
question asked at a grain the player does not build at.

## The call this needs
SELECTION.md's repeat-click cycle is battle, unit, province, building, tile. If the province
is a SECTION of the tile element rather than a kind of its own, does the cycle still stop at
a province rung, or does that rung dissolve? Dissolving it is the cleaner reading of 'bundled
into', and it costs the only gesture that selects a province without selecting a tile - which
matters because the province is the march target and the render unit. Ben's call.

## Why it is worth doing beyond the tidy
The band's RESTING state is roughly 90% empty (NR-593) and it is the state the band is in most
of the time. A longer accordion does not fix that on its own, but it is the same surface and
the same pass, and the two should be settled together rather than in sequence.

## RULED (Ben, 2026-08-24, the Sprint 17b design form)
> Province rung: **Dissolve the rung.**

The repeat-click cycle loses its province stop. The cycle becomes battle, unit, building, tile - and the province is reached as a SECTION of the tile element, which is the clean reading of 'bundled into' and the one that makes the accordion worth building.

**The consequence, stated rather than discovered later.** The province is the march target and the render unit, and after this there is no gesture that selects a province WITHOUT also selecting a tile. That is acceptable because every tile carries its province in the accordion, so the province is never unreachable - but any code that assumed a province-only selection state (`ui_state::selected_province` set with `selected_entity` null) has to keep working when both are set. The march-order path is the one to check first.

`verify.select_province` writes exactly that province-only tuple, so the harness hook and the gesture will diverge after this. Either the hook follows the gesture, or the scripts that use it are testing a state a player can no longer reach.

items.title: The minimap touches the screen edges instead of floating a few pixels short
items.design:
## Ben's words
> "Minimap needs to touch the edges of the screen, rather than popping out a bit."

## Already claimed once, and it is not true on screen
BL-312 (minimap flush edges) is marked **complete** at v0.1.1 - 'minimap wraps flush to the
canvas edges instead of floating with a margin gap' - and the 2026-08-24 shell captures show
it still inset, with a sliver of canvas visible to its left and short of the bottom-right
corner. Either the fix regressed, or 'flush to the CANVAS edge' was never the same claim as
'flush to the SCREEN edge'. Measure which before changing anything: a regression and an
unmet claim want different fixes, and the difference is recorded rather than guessed.

Beside it, the legend work (BL-566, legend inside minimap) already carries 'the minimap runs
to the screen edge' as part of its own ruling from 2026-08-22, so this is the second time the
same instruction has been given.

## Where it lives
`shell_metrics` is the one owner of screen geometry, and it exists precisely because five
sites in app.cpp each re-derived the right-column edge by hand and drifted 8px apart. Any fix
goes there, not at the call site.
items.completion_note: Complete 2026-08-24 (27d0aed8). right_chrome_left drops its margin so every occupant of the column shares the screen edge, and the minimap's bottom margin is ABSORBED into the box - its height becomes selection_band_height - so it reaches the screen foot while its top edge stays where the bottom strip's top lands. Verified by pixel measurement on the re-run shell pass: the 8px ocean strip at x=935..943 is gone, and rows 716-719 under the minimap are panel rather than canvas. The BL-312 question the item raised is answered: not a regression - 'flush to the CANVAS edge' was never the same claim as 'flush to the SCREEN edge', and the column it sits in had never moved.

items.title: The time controls touch the screen edges, on the same rule as the minimap
items.design:
## Ben's words
> "Time controls need to touch the edges of the screen too"

## One rule, two panels
The time panel and the minimap are the top and bottom of the same right-hand chrome column,
so they should share an edge rule rather than each carrying its own inset. Same owner as its
sibling item: `shell_metrics` publishes the column, both panels read it.

Worth doing in the same pass as the minimap item so the column is settled once. Worth noting
while here: the time panel publishes its own height (`ui_state::time_panel_h`) as the ceiling
the lens legend box grows down from, so moving its rect moves that legend too - which is a
reason to sequence this before the lens-chrome item, not after.
items.completion_note: Complete 2026-08-24 (27d0aed8), same change. The time panel's top edge is now y=0 and its right edge is the screen edge, which is where the profile tile and header already sat - measured before and after. pinned_panel_rect follows it up by one margin.

items.title: National borders extend their colour inwards instead of diffusing - and the nation lens retires
items.design:
## Ben's words
> "National borders should not diffuse together, instead they should borders extending their
> colour inwards. With this, we can drop the nation lens"

## The claim
A nation reads as a **bordered region**, not as a tinted field: the colour lives at the
boundary and falls off inwards, so two neighbours meeting never blend into a third colour
that belongs to neither. That is what makes the read always-on affordable - a border band
leaves the middle of a territory free for terrain, texture and whatever lens is active, which
a full-territory tint cannot do. Roads already work this way: drawn always, not behind a lens.

**So the Country lens dissolves rather than being deleted.** Its content becomes chrome.

## This overturns part of a designed item
BL-511 (province as render unit) is designed-and-unbuilt and specifies 'province-grain canvas
with **softened** borders'. Softening is the diffusion Ben is rejecting. The two cannot both
stand; newest-dated wins, so this item carries the border treatment and BL-511's remaining
content is the province-grain render, not its edge style.

## The call this needs
The Country lens is not only a wash - it is a **selection route**. LENSES.md's per-lens
routing table sends a hovered tile under that lens to its owning nation, and thence to the
Nation ledger. Dropping the lens removes the only path to a nation's ledger. Either the route
moves onto the always-on border (click a border, get the nation), or the nation ledger is
reached some other way. Ben's call, and it must be answered before the lens is removed rather
than after.

## RULED (Ben, 2026-08-24, the Sprint 17b design form)
> Nation ledger route: **Click the border itself.**

The always-on border band becomes the target. This is the answer that keeps the item coherent rather than bolting a replacement route somewhere else: the border is what now CARRIES the nation on screen, so it is the thing that should open it. A rail slot would have put a nation behind a menu while its territory sat under the pointer, and routing through the province card would have made the nation reachable only via a grain the player may not care about.

**What it needs.** A hit-test band along the border with real width - the drawn stroke is a line and a line is not clickable at play zoom - plus a hover read that says which nation before the click commits. It slots into LENSES.md's per-lens routing table as a lens-agnostic rule rather than a lens row, since the border is chrome now and not a lens.

This is also the first structure-grain selection in the shell, so it is the pattern BL-603 generalises. Build it as the general case, not as a nation special case.

items.title: Every lens selector and key lives in the minimap header, top right - one chrome, not two
items.design:
## Ben's words
> "When we use lenses, for example 'Resource deposits' needs a selection element. This
> selection element for lenses should always fit in the header for the minimap, at the top
> right corner."

## There are two legend chromes today and one of them is invisible
LENSES.md documents both. **Count-driven keys** (Country, Market, Reach, Supply-routes) live
in the right chrome column above the minimap, collapsed by default. **Gradient-bar keys**
(Resource, Production, Scarcity, Population, Industry, Opportunity, Continent) are anchored
**flush-left of the minimap**, vertically centred on it - which is inside the rect the
always-open Selection band occupies.

Measured 2026-08-24 (NR-601): six of those seven are DRAWN AND BURIED. The Population key
renders 'Workforce efficiency / low ... high' and shows through the band as a ghost at roughly
a tenth of its contrast. Only the Continent key escapes, because it alone was moved to the
foreground draw list with an opaque fill (BL-376) - one of seven was fixed and the collision
was never generalised. Nothing had ever captured the other six to notice.

So this item is not only a tidy: **it is how six lenses get a readable key at all.**

## Provenance
This is the third dated ruling on the same region and it supersedes the earlier two.
BL-533 (legend in minimap quadrant) moved legends off the canvas into the right column;
BL-566 (legend inside minimap) revised that to put them INSIDE the minimap box with the full
width hosting the lens dropdown. Ben's 2026-08-24 wording - header, top right corner - is the
current one. The selector and the key share the home; one lens draws at most one key, so one
region serves all of them.

## Sequence
After the minimap and time-panel edge items, since both move the rect this region is measured
against.

items.title: Under a lens, hover and selection pivot to the whole structure the lens is about
items.design:
## Ben's words
> "When a lens reveals any large structure, the selection should pivot to the entire
> structure, and no longer provinces. So for the market lens, the entire market gets
> highlighted on mouse over, and clicking opens up our market ledger for that market."

## Half of this is already settled design, and that is the useful part
LENSES.md carries a per-lens selection routing table settled 2026-06-15: 'the active lens does
not only re-skin the canvas, it DEFINES what the pointer resolves to'. Market already routes
to the Market Ledger, Corporation to the Balance Ledger, Country to the Nation ledger. So the
principle is not new and does not need arguing.

What is new is that the rule is currently **invisible and sub-structural**. It resolves a
target and routes a click; it does not tell the player what the target IS before they commit,
and it resolves at tile-or-province grain rather than at the grain of the thing the lens
draws. This item makes it both visible and whole-structure:
  * **Hover highlights the entire structure.** Under the Market lens the whole catchment
    lights, not the hex. The player sees the unit of meaning before clicking it.
  * **Selection takes that structure**, and stops falling back to the province.

## What counts as a structure, per lens
The render half partly exists already, which is what makes this affordable - several lenses
draw contiguous regions today and the highlight can reuse the same region walk:
  * Market -> the catchment (already a per-market tint)
  * Resource -> the contiguous deposit (already a flat fill)
  * Corporation -> the corp's holdings on this body
  * Country -> the nation's territory (see the border item - the lens itself is retiring)
  * Continent -> the plate (already a per-plate tint)
  * Supply / Supply-routes -> the lane, which is already the drawn thing

Lenses whose subject IS the tile keep tile grain. With the two per-tile value lenses retiring
in a sibling item, what remains is close to a clean split: every surviving lens either draws a
structure or draws the tile, and the selection grain follows the drawing.

## Difficulty
A 5 because it touches hover resolution, selection resolution, the highlight render and every
lens's region walk. Worth breaking down before promotion.

items.title: Retire the Opportunity and Production lenses
items.design:
## Ben's words
> "Retire the opportunity lens and the production intensity lens"

## What goes
Both are per-tile value surfaces on the bar: Opportunity draws a red-to-green mark per tile
for catchment demand-gap rank, Production a red-yellow-green intensity tint against the body
mean. Removing them takes their `overlay_mode` values, their keys, their rows in LENSES.md's
roster, rung-applicability and selection-routing tables, and their entries in the action
dictionary. The lens-cycle modulus derives from the enum sentinel, so the bar re-numbers
itself without a hand-kept count.

## Two things to decide rather than assume
  * **Production has a Circumplanetary rung** - a per-body output-throughput badge - which is
    a different read from the planetary intensity tint and is not obviously covered by the
    same objection. Does it retire with the lens, or survive as body-level chrome?
  * **The ambient opportunity read** (BL-086) is a separate always-on cue, not this lens.
    Confirm it is untouched.

## Why this is cheap and why it is worth doing now
Every lens carries a permanent cost: a slot on the bar, a row in three tables, a key, and a
selection-routing rule that the structure-pivot item would otherwise have to answer for. Two
retirements shrink the surface the lens rebuild has to cover, so this lands BEFORE the pivot
work rather than after it.
